citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

citations.quote:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff, second-countable smooth $n$-manifold without boundary. In a smooth chart $x=(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, a smooth density is written $\phi_x(x)|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$. On a coordinate change $y=\psi(x)$ its coefficient transforms by
$$ \phi_y(y)=\phi_x(\psi^{-1}(y))\,|\det D\psi^{-1}(y)|. $$
A compactly supported smooth density is one whose support (the closure of the set where its coefficient is nonzero) is compact in $M$. For compact $K\subset M$, let $\mathcal D_K(M;|\Lambda^nT^*M|)$ be the complex vector space of smooth densities supported in $K$. For every chart $x:U\to\Omega$, compact $L\subset U$, and integer $r\ge0$, give this space the seminorm
$$p_{x,L,r}(\omega)=\max_{|\alpha|\le r}\sup_{z\in x(L)}|\partial^\alpha\phi_x(z)|.$$
An empty supremum is zero. These seminorms define the fixed-support locally convex topology. On the union $\mathcal D(M;|\Lambda^nT^*M|)=\bigcup_{K\text{ compact}}\mathcal D_K(M;|\Lambda^nT^*M|)$, take all seminorms whose restriction to every fixed-support space is continuous; their finite intersections of open seminorm balls and translates define the test-density topology. Thus it is the finest locally convex topology making every fixed-support inclusion continuous, as in the Euclidean test-function topology. This specifies the locally convex inductive limit without choosing an exhaustion.

A scalar distribution on $M$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on this space, with bilinear pairing $\langle u,\omega\rangle$. Write $\mathcal D'(M)$ for these distributions. The support of $u$ is the complement of the union of open sets on which it annihilates every supported test density; $\mathcal E'(M)$ denotes those with compact support. For $x:U\to\Omega$, its coordinate representative is defined for $f\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ by
$$\langle u_x,f\rangle=\langle u,\widetilde{x^*(f|dz^1\cdots dz^n|)}\rangle,$$
where the tilde extends the density by zero outside $U$. This extension is smooth because the support is compact in $U$. On each fixed support its derivatives in any other chart are bounded by finitely many derivatives of $f$, by the chain and product rules on compact sets; hence the extension map is continuous for the specified topologies and $u_x$ is a Euclidean distribution. In dimension zero derivatives have order zero and the density determinant is one. On a product manifold use the same definition with product densities. For a smooth diffeomorphism $f:N\to M$, define $f_*\omega=(f^{-1})^*\omega$ for test densities, using the displayed absolute-Jacobian rule. Define its distributional pullback by $\langle f^*u,\omega\rangle=\langle u,f_*\omega\rangle$. Compact supports are mapped to compact supports, and the same compact derivative estimates prove continuity. This includes coordinate changes and interchange of factors of a product.

A complex-linear functional $u:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathbb C$ is a distribution if and only if, for every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$, there are an integer $m_K\ge0$ and a finite constant $C_K\ge0$ such that
$$|u(\varphi)|\le C_K p_{m_K}(\varphi)\qquad(\varphi\in\mathcal D_K).$$
The quantifiers are $\forall K\,\exists(m_K,C_K)$; no simultaneous selection of witnesses is asserted or needed. The equivalence holds in ZF.

Give $C^\infty(\Omega)$ the topology generated by $q_{K,m}(f)=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_K|\partial^\alpha f|$ for compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ and $m\ge0$. A compactly supported distribution $u$ has a unique continuous complex-linear extension to this space, given by
$$\widetilde u(f)=u(\chi f),$$
where $\chi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is any cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}u$. The result is independent of $\chi$. The extension vanishes on every smooth function zero near the support. No Hahn–Banach or choice axiom is needed.

Assume Countable Choice.  Let $v\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n)$ have compact
support, let $\widetilde v\in\mathcal S'$ be its canonical extension, and let
$\chi\in\mathcal D$ equal one on a neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}v$.
Then $\mathcal F\widetilde v$ is the regular tempered distribution represented
by

$$V(\xi)=\left\langle v_x,\chi(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}\right\rangle.$$

The function $V$ is independent of $\chi$, is smooth, and for every
multi-index $\alpha$ there are $C_\alpha,m_\alpha$ with
$|\partial^\alpha V(\xi)|\leq C_\alpha(1+|\xi|)^{m_\alpha}$.  Consequently
multiplication by $V$ is continuous on $\mathcal S$ and, by transpose, on
$\mathcal S'$ in both dual topologies.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $u\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)$, using the local distribution convention of [[def-qftx-distributions-on-smooth-manifolds]]. For $p\in\Omega$ and $\xi\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$, call $(p,\xi)$ regular for $u$ if there are $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\chi=1$ near $p$ and an open cone $\Gamma\subseteq\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ containing $\xi$ such that for every integer $N\ge0$,
$$ \sup_{\eta\in\Gamma}(1+|\eta|)^N\left|\left\langle u,\chi(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\eta}|dx^1\cdots dx^n|\right\rangle\right|<\infty. $$
The local wavefront set $\operatorname{WF}_\Omega(u)$ is the complement of these regular pairs in $T^*\Omega\setminus0$, with the standard cotangent coordinates $(p,\xi)$. A cone is invariant under multiplication by positive scalars. This is a chart-level definition; this item makes no assertion about its behavior under a change of coordinates.

citations.quote: For a distribution $u$ on a smooth manifold, the chartwise rapid-decay definition of its wavefront set is independent of the chart: if $y=\psi(x)$, its covector coordinates satisfy $\eta=(D\psi(x))^{-T}\xi$. The resulting $\operatorname{WF}(u)$ is closed and conic in $T^*M\setminus0$. For distributions $u,v$ and a smooth diffeomorphism $\psi$, one has $\operatorname{WF}(u+v)\subseteq\operatorname{WF}(u)\cup\operatorname{WF}(v)$ and $\operatorname{WF}(\psi^*u)=\psi^*\operatorname{WF}(u)$. Finally, $\operatorname{WF}(u)=\varnothing$ exactly when $u$ is represented by a smooth scalar function in every chart.

citations.quote:
For $\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$, the map

$$x\longmapsto T_x\varphi,\qquad (T_x\varphi)(y)=\varphi(x-y),$$

is $C^\infty$ as a map from $\mathbb R^n$ to Schwartz space, with
$\partial_x^\gamma T_x\varphi=T_x(\partial^\gamma\varphi)$.  This clause holds
in ZF.

Assume Countable Choice for the following integral clause.  Let $r\geq1$ and
let $H:\mathbb R^r\to\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ be continuous in every Schwartz
seminorm.  Suppose each $\partial_y^\beta H(t,y)$ is jointly measurable and,
for every $\alpha,\beta$, there is $g_{\alpha\beta}\in L^1(\mathbb R^r)$ such
that

$$p_{\alpha\beta}(H(t))\leq g_{\alpha\beta}(t)$$

for almost every $t$.  Then
$G(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^r}H(t,y)\,dt$ belongs to $\mathcal S$, derivatives pass
under the integral, and every $u\in\mathcal S'$ satisfies

$$\left\langle u,\int H(t)\,dt\right\rangle =\int\langle u,H(t)\rangle\,dt.$$

All integrals in this clause are Lebesgue integrals.

citations.quote:
Let $r,n\ge1$ be integers, let $X\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ and $Y\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $u\in\mathcal D'(Y)$, and let $F\in C^\infty(X\times Y;\mathbb C)$. Suppose that for each compact $H\subseteq X$ there is compact $K\subseteq Y$ with $\operatorname{supp}_y F(x,\cdot)\subseteq K$ for every $x\in H$. Then $a(x)=u(F(x,\cdot))$ is smooth and $\partial_x^\alpha a(x)=u(\partial_x^\alpha F(x,\cdot))$.

Assume Countable Choice for the following integral clause. For every compact measurable $E\subseteq X$, the function $G(y)=\int_E F(x,y)\,dx$ is a test in $\mathcal D(Y)$, its $y$ derivatives pass under the integral, and $u(G)=\int_E u(F(x,\cdot))\,dx$. Integrals here are Lebesgue integrals. The smoothness and differentiation claims hold in ZF; Countable Choice supplies Lebesgue measure for the integral clause. Neither clause uses tensor products or distributional mollification.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;
2. for $\nu$-almost every $y$, the section $f^y$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$;
3. after assigning the value $0$ on the exceptional parameter sets, the
   section-integral functions are integrable; and
4. the three integrals agree:
$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. If $f : V \to \mathbb C$ belongs to $L^1(\lambda_n)$,
then
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
(The Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$)), and let $a_i \le b_i$ be reals for $i<n$. Write

$$R^{\circ} := \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_i < x_i < b_i \text{ for every } i<n \,\}, \qquad \overline{R} := [a,b] = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_i \le x_i \le b_i \text{ for every } i<n \,\}$$

(Axis-parallel rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^m$ and their volume). Then $R^{\circ}$ is open and
$\overline{R}$ is closed, so both are Borel and Lebesgue measurable, and **every**
set $R$ with $R^{\circ} \subseteq R \subseteq \overline{R}$ is Lebesgue
measurable with

$$\lambda_n(R) \;=\; \prod_{i<n}(b_i-a_i).$$

In particular this covers the four one-dimensional face conventions in each
coordinate — the open box, the closed box $[a,b]$, the half-open box
$B(a,b) = \prod_{i<n}(a_i,b_i]$ of Half-open boxes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and their volume, and every mixture of
them, in any combination of coordinates — and it gives measure $0$ to all of them
whenever $a_i = b_i$ for some $i<n$. For a half-open box with infinite
parameters the value is already
$\lambda_n(B) = \operatorname{vol}(B)$ (Assuming countable choice, $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is a sigma-algebra containing every elementary set and $\lambda_n$ is a complete measure extending elementary volume).

derivations.claim: We first specify two elementary Fourier estimates used with uniform constants. A compact smooth amplitude $a$ has $|\widehat a(\eta)|\le C_q(1+|\eta|)^{-q}$: for $|\eta|\ge1$ integrate repeatedly in a coordinate with $|\eta_i|\ge|\eta|/\sqrt n$, and use its bounded support for $|\eta|\le1$. If compact distributions $v_j$ share an order-$m$ bound, [F2] gives $|\widehat v_j(\eta)|\le C(1+|\eta|)^m$ uniformly. Multiplication by $a$ corresponds to convolution with $\widehat a$, by [F4]. Uniform rapid decay in a cone transfers to every smaller closed cone under this multiplication: split the convolution into input frequencies in an intermediate regular cone and its complement. In the first region either that frequency is at least half the output size, giving its rapid bound, or the Schwartz factor has size at least half the output size. In the complement, angular separation gives a Schwartz-factor argument bounded below by a positive constant times the sum of both frequency sizes. Taking the decay exponent above $m+n+q+1$ makes each tail integrable and bounds the convolution by $C_q(1+|\eta|)^{-q}$. This proves also smooth-factor wavefront containment, with uniform bounds for families. The parameter-pairing lemma justifies the convolution before the estimates; all resulting integrals are absolutely convergent.

Here is the needed nonstationary estimate, including its dependence on the amplitude. On a fixed compact coordinate set let $\Phi(x;\eta,\xi)=f(x)\cdot\eta-x\cdot\xi$, put $R=|\eta|+|\xi|\ge1$, and suppose $|
abla_x\Phi|\ge cR$ throughout the amplitude support. Every fixed $x$ derivative of $
abla\Phi$ is at most $C_\alpha R$. Differentiating the quotient shows that every fixed derivative of $b=
abla\Phi/(2\pi i|
abla\Phi|^2)$ is at most $C'_\alpha R^{-1}$. The operator $L=b\cdot
abla_x$ satisfies $L e^{2\pi i\Phi}=e^{2\pi i\Phi}$. Repeated integration by parts gives $$\left|\int e^{2\pi i\Phi}a(x)\,dxight|\le C_q R^{-q}\max_{|\alpha|\le q}\sup|\partial^\alpha a|.$$ Indeed $L^*a=-\sum_i\partial_i(b_i a)$, and induction gives a finite sum of derivatives of $a$ through order $q$ times products of $q$ coefficient derivatives, each contributing $R^{-1}$. Compact support removes boundary terms. Constants depend only on finitely many derivatives of $f$, the compact set and $c$, and are uniform for every frequency in the specified region. The same proof with $\xi=0$ applies to $f(x)\cdot\eta$.

We construct the smooth approximants rather than assume a distributional regularization theorem. By [F5] choose $b\ge0$ compactly supported and equal to one on a neighborhood of a closed box of positive volume inside the unit ball. Rescale its support into the unit ball. By [F6], $0<\int b<\infty$; put $\rho=b/\int b$ and $\rho_\epsilon(z)=\epsilon^{-n}\rho(z/\epsilon)$. For a compactly supported distribution $v$, define $v_\epsilon(y)=\langle v(z),\rho_\epsilon(y-z)|dz|\rangle$. It is smooth by [F4], supported in the $\epsilon$-neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}v$, and has common compact support for $0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$. Pairing against a test $h$ and using [F4] gives $\langle v_\epsilon,h\rangle=\langle v,h_\epsilon\rangle$, where $h_\epsilon(z)=\int\rho(w)h(z+\epsilon w)dw$. Every derivative of $h_\epsilon-h$ tends uniformly to zero on the common compact support, by uniform continuity of the corresponding derivative of $h$. The finite-order bound proves weak convergence and a common order bound, because the averaging bounds every derivative seminorm of $h_\epsilon$ by the corresponding seminorm of $h$ on a fixed enlarged compact. The same interchange, or Fourier testing, gives $$\widehat{v_\epsilon}(\eta)=\widehat\rho(\epsilon\eta)\widehat v(\eta),\qquad |\widehat\rho(\epsilon\eta)|\le\int\rho=1.$$ Hence all polynomial and regular-cone bounds for $v$ are uniform in $\epsilon$. For a smaller local cutoff $a$, first choose $b_0=1$ near its support, inside a wavefront-regularity localization. For sufficiently small $\epsilon$, $a(\rho_\epsilon*v)=a(\rho_\epsilon*(b_0v))$; step 1.1 gives the uniform regular-cone bound. The finitely many initial terms of a sequence $\epsilon_j\downarrow0$ are smooth and have their own finite rapid bounds. Compactness and finite subdivision into regular base/cone patches handle any compact cutoff/cone pair disjoint from $\operatorname{WF}(v)$. Thus these approximants are controlled on each smaller patch.

Fix $x_0\in N$ and use one source chart and one target chart about $y_0=f(x_0)$, of positive dimensions for now. On their unit frequency spheres set $K_0=\{\eta:df_{x_0}^T\eta=0\}$. It is compact and disjoint from the compact fiber $\Gamma_{y_0}\cap S^{m-1}$. Choose an open conic neighborhood $V$ of $K_0$ with closure of directions still disjoint from that fiber. Closedness of $\Gamma$ implies that the same disjointness holds over a sufficiently small target neighborhood: otherwise points of $\Gamma$ approaching $y_0$, with directions in the compact closure, have a subsequence with a forbidden limit. Outside $V$, compactness gives $|df_{x_0}^T\eta|\ge2c|\eta|$; shrink the source chart so $|df_x^T\eta|\ge c|\eta|$ there. Shrink again so its image lies in the target neighborhood and choose its target cutoff $\beta$ supported there. If $K_0$ is empty take $V$ empty. Localized Fourier transforms $\widehat{\beta u}$ are rapidly decreasing on $V$: for each compact set of directions in $V$, the regularity witnesses over $\operatorname{supp}\beta$ give a finite base cover and cutoff decomposition; step 1.1 transfers the bounds, and a finite direction cover gives one bound for each order. Choose $V$ initially with closure inside this regular neighborhood, so the bounds hold on its whole set of directions. Only finitely many witnesses are used for each such estimate.

On a compact source test support $H$ inside this small patch, choose $\beta=1$ near $f(H)$ and write $v=\beta u$. For $\omega=a(x)|dx|$ define $$T_a(\eta)=\int e^{2\pi i f(x)\cdot\eta}a(x)dx,\qquad P_f(v)(\omega)=\int\widehat v(\eta)T_a(\eta)d\eta.$$ On $V$, $\widehat v$ decreases arbitrarily fast and $|T_a|\le\operatorname{vol}(H)\sup|a|$. Off $V$, step 1.2 with $\xi=0$ gives $|T_a(\eta)|\le C_q(1+|\eta|)^{-q}p_q(a)$. Take $q>m+m_v+1$, where $m$ is the target dimension and $m_v$ is a finite-order exponent from [F2]. The integrals are absolutely convergent, with $|P_f(v)(\omega)|\le C p_q(a)$. This proves fixed-support continuity, hence a distribution by [F1]. If $v_j\to v$ is controlled, their common finite-order and regular-cone bounds give the same integrable majorant. Weak convergence gives $\widehat v_j(\eta)\to\widehat v(\eta)$ for each fixed $\eta$, so dominated convergence proves $P_f(v_j)(\omega)\to P_f(v)(\omega)$, with a uniform fixed-support order bound. For smooth $v$, Fourier inversion and absolutely integrable Fubini identify the value with $\int v(f(x))\omega(x)$.

We prove the output cone estimate with uniform bounds, needed also for controlled limits. Fix an output direction $\xi_0$ at $x_0$ outside $f^*\Gamma$. Shrink the source base patch and its output cone $C$ about $\xi_0$. There is a target singular-direction cone $G$ containing every direction of $\Gamma$ over the target cutoff support such that for $\eta\in G$, $\xi\in C$ and $x$ in the source patch, $$|df_x^T\eta-\xi|\ge c_1(|\eta|+|\xi|).$$ To see this, normalize $|\eta|+|\xi|=1$. A sequence contradicting the bound has a convergent frequency subsequence and base limit. If the output frequency limit were zero, local transversality from step 2.2 forces the input frequency limit to be zero; if the input limit were zero the equation forces the output limit to be zero. Both contradict normalization. Otherwise the limit is a covector in $f^*\Gamma$ with output direction in the chosen excluded closed cone. Closedness and compactness therefore give the separation after shrinking; choose a slightly larger closed input cone still satisfying it. The complement of $G$ is regular for the localized input. To Fourier transform a compact output localization replace $a$ in step 3.1 by $a(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}$. On $G$, apply step 1.2 and the polynomial input bound. Its integral is at most $C_q(1+|\xi|)^{-q+m+m_v}$ after increasing $q$. Off $G$, use a uniform bound $B$ for $df_x^T$. For $|\eta|\le|\xi|/(2\max(1,B))$, the phase is nonstationary and the same estimate applies. For the remaining regular input frequencies, the bound on $T_a$ and arbitrary input decay give $C_N(1+|\xi|)^{-N+m}$ after integration. Taking these exponents arbitrarily large proves rapid output decay on $C$. The estimates use only common input bounds, so they hold uniformly for controlled sequences. The set $f^*\Gamma$ is closed locally away from the zero section: transversality bounds $|\eta|$ by a constant times $|df_x^T\eta|$ on $\Gamma$ over a smaller compact patch, allowing the same compactness argument. Thus the output weak limits and these uniform bounds give exactly the claimed controlled convergence.

The formula is independent of the allowed target cutoff. For two cutoffs equal to one near $f(H)$, first work inside one of the small target neighborhoods of step 2.2. Their difference times $u$ is a compact distribution $w$ zero on a neighborhood of the compact set $f(H)$. Its mollifications from step 2.1 vanish at every $f(x)$, $x\in H$, for sufficiently small $\epsilon$, since their supports expand by at most $\epsilon$ and the two closed compact sets have positive Euclidean distance. Their ordinary smooth pullbacks therefore pair to zero with $\omega$. The controlled continuity in step 3.1 makes $P_f(w)(\omega)=0$. If the two originally allowed target neighborhoods differ, insert a third cutoff supported in their overlap and equal to one near the image of a smaller source support; compare with it in each neighborhood and use a finite decomposition of $\omega$. This also proves locality and independence of extensions outside the target chart.

Controlled convergence is invariant under a smooth change of coordinates. For completeness, the Fourier estimate is the one for a diffeomorphism, not an assumed arbitrary-map pullback. In source coordinates $y=\psi(z)$, the localized transformed Fourier value pairs $v_j$ with $a(\psi(z))|\det D\psi(z)|e^{-2\pi i\psi(z)\cdot\eta}$. Insert a cutoff equal to one on this compact support and use Fourier inversion [F4]. The resulting phase is $z\cdot\zeta-\psi(z)\cdot\eta$. In the near-stationary region $\zeta$ is comparable to $\eta$ and lies in a regular source cone whenever the transformed compact base/output cone avoids the transported $\Gamma$; there use the uniform regular bounds and a polynomial volume estimate. On the complementary region $|\zeta-D\psi(z)^T\eta|\ge c(|\zeta|+|\eta|)$; step 1.2 and the uniform polynomial bound give arbitrary rapid decay after integration. This is precisely the chart-invariance estimate with constants uniform in $j$. Common finite-order bounds transfer by the finite chain/product rules for compactly supported test densities, and weak convergence transfers because diffeomorphism pullback is already defined by the density transpose. Hence the same smooth approximants from step 2.1, expressed in either target chart, are controlled. Both local candidates in step 3.1 are their limits and equal the same ordinary smooth pullback at every stage. They are therefore equal. A change of source chart similarly gives the same smooth integrals by the absolute-Jacobian substitution in [F6], followed by the controlled limit. This proves coordinate covariance of the constructed scalar distribution and compatibility with the previously defined diffeomorphism pullback.

We now glue; no assumption that $f(\operatorname{supp}\omega)$ fits one chart is made. Cover the compact support of a test density by finitely many small source patches of step 2.2. Shrink the covering patches still covering that support, take compact smooth cutoffs $b_i$ supported in the original patches and equal to one on the smaller ones, and put $s=\sum_i b_i$. It is positive near the test support. With another compact cutoff $h=1$ there and supported where $s>0$, set $a_i=hb_i/s$ there and zero elsewhere. They are smooth, subordinate, and sum to one near the test support. Define $\langle f^*u,\omega\rangle=\sum_i P_{f,i}(u)(a_i\omega)$. On an overlap the two terms are equal: shrink around each point to a common source patch and a target chart inside the two target-chart overlap, use step 4.2 for cutoffs and step 5.1 for coordinates, and decompose a compact overlap test into finitely many such patches. Two partitions now give the same answer by the double sum on $a_i a'_j\omega$. This proves linearity, independence and compatibility with restriction. For each fixed compact support choose this finite cover once. Each local pairing has a finite seminorm estimate by step 3.1; multiplication by the fixed $a_i$ is bounded by finitely many compact derivative seminorms. Their finite sum is continuous on that fixed-support space, and the test-density topology in [F1] gives a global distribution. Local estimates in step 4.1 give its wavefront bound and controlled sequential continuity.

If a source or target coordinate dimension is zero, every local distribution there is a scalar function, and the relevant local map is an ordinary smooth map from or to a point. For a zero-dimensional source, transversality forces the target distribution to be smooth near its image point, by [F3], so evaluation is defined; for a zero-dimensional target its local scalar pulls back as a constant. The finite-test gluing above handles zero-dimensional components, and an empty source has only the zero test space and its unique distribution. Zero inputs pull back to zero. Nonproper $f$ has required no extra hypothesis: each construction used only a compact source test support and its compact image. Finally any other rule agreeing on smooth inputs and obeying the stated controlled sequential continuity agrees on each small patch by the actual approximants of step 2.1, hence agrees globally by step 6.1. All coverings and comparisons for one test use finite choice only; [A1] enters exactly through the declared Fourier and Lebesgue suppliers.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $M$ be an oriented, time-oriented, globally hyperbolic smooth Lorentzian $n$-manifold without boundary, $n\ge2$, with signature $(-,+,\ldots,+)$. A cotangent vector is future or past causal when its metric dual belongs to the corresponding closed causal tangent cone. For $r\ge1$, let $\overline V_\pm^r\subset T^*M^r\setminus0$ consist of tuples $(x_1,\ldots,x_r;\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_r)$ such that every $\xi_j$ is either zero or future causal for $+$, respectively past causal for $-$, and the total tuple is nonzero. The wavefront set used below is the set of nonzero cotangent tuples where compactly localized Fourier transforms fail rapid decay in every conic neighborhood.

A compactly supported polynomial functional is a finite expression
$$ F(\phi)=\sum_{m=0}^{N}\left\langle f_m,\phi^{\otimes m}\mu_g^{\otimes m}\right\rangle, $$
where $\phi\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$, $f_m\in\mathcal E'(M^m)$ is symmetric under permutations of its $m$ variables, $\mu_g$ is the metric density fixed by the Lorentzian metric, and the pairing is defined by inserting a compactly supported cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}f_m$ in the smooth factor. Its $r$th functional derivative $F^{(r)}(\phi)\in\mathcal E'(M^r)$ is specified, for a test density $\omega$ on $M^r$, by
$$ \left\langle F^{(r)}(\phi),\omega\right\rangle =\sum_{m=r}^{N}\frac{m!}{(m-r)!} \left\langle f_m,\omega\otimes\phi^{\otimes(m-r)}\mu_g^{\otimes(m-r)}\right\rangle, $$
where a compactly supported cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}f_m$ is inserted in the smooth $\phi$ factors. Expanding the finite polynomial shows that this kernel represents the directional derivative in smooth compactly supported real directions. The functional is microcausal when
$$ \operatorname{WF}(F^{(r)}(\phi))\cap(\overline V_+^r\cup\overline V_-^r)=\varnothing $$
for every $r\ge1$ and every $\phi\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$. Write $\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(M)$ for this class, including constants.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $M,N$ be Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifolds without boundary, let $f:N\to M$ be smooth, and let $\Gamma\subset T^*M\setminus0$ be closed and conic. Put
$$N_f=\{(f(x),\eta):\eta\ne0,\ df_x^T\eta=0\}.$$
If $\Gamma\cap N_f=\varnothing$, every $u\in\mathcal D'(M)$ with $\operatorname{WF}(u)\subset\Gamma$ has a canonical scalar-distribution pullback $f^*u$. It agrees with $u\circ f$ for smooth scalar functions, commutes with restriction to open subsets, is independent of all coordinate charts and support cutoffs, and satisfies
$$\operatorname{WF}(f^*u)\subset f^*\Gamma:=\{(x,df_x^T\eta):(f(x),\eta)\in\Gamma\}.$$
In particular the same assertion holds with $\Gamma=\operatorname{WF}(u)$. A nonproper map and a test whose image meets several target charts are allowed.

The following precise local convergence property is part of the assertion. Call $u_j\to u$ **controlled relative to $\Gamma$** when all these distributions have wavefront sets in $\Gamma$, they converge on every fixed test density, on each fixed compact test support they share one finite derivative-order bound, and, in every chart, for every compact smooth cutoff $a$ and closed cone $C$ with $(\operatorname{supp}a\times C)\cap\Gamma=\varnothing$, one has
$$\sup_j\sup_{\eta\in C}(1+|\eta|)^q|\widehat{a u_j}(\eta)|<\infty\qquad(q=0,1,\ldots).$$
An empty cone imposes no condition. Then $f^*u_j\to f^*u$ is controlled relative to $f^*\Gamma$ locally, with common support bounds whenever the input supports and the relevant source test supports are fixed. On a compact coordinate patch, compactly supported smooth mollifications of a localized distribution give such an approximating sequence on every smaller patch. Consequently the pullback is uniquely determined by its smooth values and this controlled sequential continuity. This statement uses the explicitly defined convergence property, rather than assuming a general spectral or locally convex extension principle.

Let $u\in\mathcal D'(M)$, where $M$ is a smooth manifold. For a smooth map $f:N\to M$, define its nonzero conormal set by
$$ N_f=\{(f(x),\eta)\in T^*M\setminus0: df_x^T\eta=0\}. $$
If $\operatorname{WF}(u)\cap N_f=\varnothing$, there is a distributional pullback $f^*u\in\mathcal D'(N)$ and
$$ \operatorname{WF}(f^*u)\subseteq \{(x,df_x^T\eta):(f(x),\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(u)\}. $$
For $u,v\in\mathcal D'(M)$, if there is no nonzero covector $\eta$ with both $(x,\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(u)$ and $(x,-\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(v)$ at the same $x$, their product is defined by $uv=\Delta^*(u\otimes v)$, where $\Delta(x)=(x,x)$. It agrees with pointwise multiplication when $u,v$ are smooth and satisfies
$$ \operatorname{WF}(uv)\subseteq \{(x,\eta+\zeta):(x,\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(u)\cup0_M,\ (x,\zeta)\in\operatorname{WF}(v)\cup0_M,\ \eta+\zeta\ne0\}. $$
Here $0_M$ is the zero section. If $\pi:X\times Y\to X$ is a coordinate projection, $\nu$ is a smooth positive density on $Y$, and $t\in\mathcal E'(X\times Y)$, define $\pi_{*,\nu}t$ by
$$ \langle \pi_{*,\nu}t,\omega\rangle =\left\langle t,\chi(\pi^*\omega\otimes\nu)\right\rangle, $$
where $\omega$ is a compactly supported test density on $X$ and $\chi$ is a compact cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}t$. This pushforward is independent of $\chi$, compactly supported, and
$$ \operatorname{WF}(\pi_{*,\nu}t)\subseteq \{(x,\eta):\text{ for some }y,\ (x,y;\eta,0)\in\operatorname{WF}(t)\}. $$
The pullback condition is a local transversality requirement; this theorem does not define an arbitrary restriction of a singular kernel to a diagonal where the condition fails.

Assume Countable Choice.  Let $v\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n)$ have compact
support, let $\widetilde v\in\mathcal S'$ be its canonical extension, and let
$\chi\in\mathcal D$ equal one on a neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}v$.
Then $\mathcal F\widetilde v$ is the regular tempered distribution represented
by

$$V(\xi)=\left\langle v_x,\chi(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}\right\rangle.$$

The function $V$ is independent of $\chi$, is smooth, and for every
multi-index $\alpha$ there are $C_\alpha,m_\alpha$ with
$|\partial^\alpha V(\xi)|\leq C_\alpha(1+|\xi|)^{m_\alpha}$.  Consequently
multiplication by $V$ is continuous on $\mathcal S$ and, by transpose, on
$\mathcal S'$ in both dual topologies.

let $H:\mathbb R^r\to\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ be continuous in every Schwartz
seminorm.  Suppose each $\partial_y^\beta H(t,y)$ is jointly measurable and,

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;
2. for $\nu$-almost every $y$, the section $f^y$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$;
3. after assigning the value $0$ on the exceptional parameter sets, the
   section-integral functions are integrable; and
4. the three integrals agree:

derivations.claim: We prove the finite-family product estimate needed for compatibility; pairwise criteria alone will not be substituted for it. The empty family has ordinary product one. In a zero-dimensional configuration chart all local distributions are scalars, so products and integrations are finite scalar operations; the following frequency argument is for $s,d\ge1$. Let $v_1,\ldots,v_s$ be localized distributions on one $d$-dimensional chart, and suppose that no tuple $\eta_j\in\Gamma_j\cup\{0\}$, not all zero, has $\sum_j\eta_j=0$, where the closed cones $\Gamma_j$ contain their wavefront directions over the compact base patch. If every $\Gamma_j$ is empty, all factors are smooth by [F3]; take $G_j=\varnothing$ and $c=1$. Every tuple of total size $R>0$ then has a regular factor of size at least $R/s$, so the first alternative below applies, and no minimum over an empty permitted set is taken. Otherwise, on $\sum_j|\eta_j|=1$ the permitted tuples form a nonempty compact set, so the norm of the sum has a positive minimum $c$. Choose slightly larger conic neighborhoods $G_j$ retaining a lower bound $c/2$ on this compact set; shrink the base patch first if the cones vary with the base point. This follows by taking a convergent subsequence of any alleged violating normalized tuples and using closedness of each wavefront set. The transforms $\widehat v_j$ have bounds $C_j(1+|\eta_j|)^{m_j}$ everywhere and arbitrary rapid bounds off $G_j$, by [F3] and [F5]. Put $R=\sum_j|\eta_j|$. For a sufficiently small fixed $\delta>0$, every frequency tuple either has an index $j$ with $\eta_j\notin G_j$ and $|\eta_j|\ge\delta R$, or satisfies $|\sum_j\eta_j|\ge cR/4$. Indeed, otherwise discard all frequencies outside their $G_j$; their total norm is below $s\delta R$, while the remaining cone frequencies have sum norm at least $(c/2)(1-s\delta)R$. Subtracting the discarded sum proves the assertion when $s\delta(1+c/2)<c/4$.

Compact pushforward is compatible with these controlled limits. For a coordinate projection $\pi(x,z)=x$ and a common compact support, multiply the smooth density in the integrated $z$ variables by one fixed compact cutoff equal to one there. Testing $\pi_*t_j$ against $h(x)|dx|$ is then testing $t_j$ against a single fixed-support smooth density. Weak convergence and a uniform finite-order bound follow directly. In local charts its output Fourier transform is the full transform of this fixed smooth localization of $t_j$ evaluated at vertical covector zero. If the output compact base/cone avoids the projected input cone with zero vertical covector, finite compact vertical covers and the uniform regular-cone bounds for $t_j$ give arbitrary rapid output decay. Thus $\pi_*t_j$ converges controlled with exactly the projected cone in [F4]. For smooth compact distributions, integration in any order agrees by ordinary Fubini; for the controlled limits the same equality follows by applying the continuous test pairings just proved. This includes output dimension zero, where pushforward is the scalar total pairing.

For a compactly supported smooth test $h$, consider $$\int_{(\mathbb R^d)^s}\left(\prod_{j=1}^s\widehat v_j(\eta_j)\right)\widehat h\!\left(-\sum_j\eta_j\right)d\eta_1\cdots d\eta_s.$$ It is absolutely convergent. In the first region of step 1.1, use arbitrary rapid decay of the indicated comparable-size regular factor and polynomial bounds for the others; in the second, use arbitrary rapid decay of $\widehat h$. For every prescribed $Q$ both bounds are at most $C_Qp_{n_Q}(h)(1+R)^{-Q}$ after increasing the rapid exponent above $Q+\sum_jm_j$; the finite region $R\le1$ has the same bound with a larger constant. Choose $Q>sd$. Integration proves a finite-seminorm distribution estimate. For smooth compact factors the value is exactly $\int h\prod_jv_j$ by Fourier inversion and absolutely integrable Fubini. Approximate every $v_j$ by the controlled smooth sequences in [F3], with independent approximation indices. Their uniform bounds give the same integrable majorant. Each Fourier factor converges pointwise, so dominated convergence identifies every joint or iterated approximation limit with this one integral. This defines a simultaneous product and proves its invariance under reordering the factors.

The preceding bounds also give the common finite-order and regular-cone estimates for all intermediate products. To check the latter, replace $h$ by $h(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}$. If an output cone avoids every nonzero sum of covectors from the selected $\Gamma_j\cup0$, compactness of normalized tuples implies that either a comparable-size factor is in a regular cone or $|\xi-\sum_j\eta_j|$ is comparable to $|\xi|+R$. Use rapid decay of that factor or of $\widehat h(\xi-\sum_j\eta_j)$ exactly as in step 2.1. Taking exponents arbitrarily large gives uniform rapid decay in that output cone. Noncancellation makes the cone sums locally closed away from zero: bounded output covectors bound the sum of the norms of input covectors, by step 1.1, and thus allow a convergent subsequence. Weak convergence on tests was already proved. Hence the intermediate products converge in the explicitly controlled sense of [F3]. For two factors this limit equals the product in [F4], because controlled tensor approximants and the diagonal pullback in [F3] have precisely that smooth limit. Group any subset first and repeat: its sum cone satisfies the next product condition whenever the full simultaneous condition holds. Controlled continuity and the common multi-frequency integral therefore prove every such iterated product agrees with the simultaneous one. These arguments are local; [F3], using the same transformed approximants and finite support partitions, makes the product cutoff- and coordinate-independent.

We prove that the Statement's matching actually satisfies the simultaneous condition. $$ \phi_y(y)=\phi_x(\psi^{-1}(y))\,|\det D\psi^{-1}(y)|. $$
A compactly supported smooth density is one whose support (the closure of the set where its coefficient is nonzero) is compact in $M$. For compact $K\subset M$, let $\mathcal D_K(M;|\Lambda^nT^*M|)$ be the complex vector space of smooth densities supported in $K$. $$p_{x,L,r}(\omega)=\max_{|\alpha|\le r}\sup_{z\in x(L)}|\partial^\alpha\phi_x(z)|.$$
An empty supremum is zero. These seminorms define the fixed-support locally convex topology. On the union $\mathcal D(M;|\Lambda^nT^*M|)=\bigcup_{K\text{ compact}}\mathcal D_K(M;|\Lambda^nT^*M|)$, take all seminorms whose restriction to every fixed-support space is continuous; their finite intersections of open seminorm balls and translates define the test-density topology. This specifies the locally convex inductive limit without choosing an exhaustion.

A scalar distribution on $M$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on this space, with bilinear pairing $\langle u,\omega\rangle$. Write $\mathcal D'(M)$ for these distributions. The support of $u$ is the complement of the union of open sets on which it annihilates every supported test density; $\mathcal E'(M)$ denotes those with compact support. $$\langle u_x,f\rangle=\langle u,\widetilde{x^*(f|dz^1\cdots dz^n|)}\rangle,$$

A cotangent vector is future or past causal when its metric dual belongs to the corresponding closed causal tangent cone. A compactly supported polynomial functional is a finite expression
$$ F(\phi)=\sum_{m=0}^{N}\left\langle f_m,\phi^{\otimes m}\mu_g^{\otimes m}\right\rangle, $$

Let $u\in\mathcal D'(M)$, where $M$ is a smooth manifold. For a smooth map $f:N\to M$, define its nonzero conormal set by
$$ N_f=\{(f(x),\eta)\in T^*M\setminus0: df_x^T\eta=0\}. $$
If $\operatorname{WF}(u)\cap N_f=\varnothing$, there is a distributional pullback $f^*u\in\mathcal D'(N)$ and
$$ \operatorname{WF}(f^*u)\subseteq \{(x,df_x^T\eta):(f(x),\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(u)\}. $$
For $u,v\in\mathcal D'(M)$, if there is no nonzero covector $\eta$ with both $(x,\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(u)$ and $(x,-\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(v)$ at the same $x$, their product is defined by $uv=\Delta^*(u\otimes v)$, where $\Delta(x)=(x,x)$. It agrees with pointwise multiplication when $u,v$ are smooth and satisfies
$$ \operatorname{WF}(uv)\subseteq \{(x,\eta+\zeta):(x,\eta)\in\operatorname{WF}(u)\cup0_M,\ (x,\zeta)\in\operatorname{WF}(v)\cup0_M,\ \eta+\zeta\ne0\}. $$
Here $0_M$ is the zero section. If $\pi:X\times Y\to X$ is a coordinate projection, $\nu$ is a smooth positive density on $Y$, and $t\in\mathcal E'(X\times Y)$, define $\pi_{*,\nu}t$ by
$$ \langle \pi_{*,\nu}t,\omega\rangle =\left\langle t,\chi(\pi^*\omega\otimes\nu)\right\rangle, $$
where $\omega$ is a compactly supported test density on $X$ and $\chi$ is a compact cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}t$. This pushforward is independent of $\chi$, compactly supported, and
$$ \operatorname{WF}(\pi_{*,\nu}t)\subseteq \{(x,\eta):\text{ for some }y,\ (x,y;\eta,0)\in\operatorname{WF}(t)\}. $$
The pullback condition is a local transversality requirement; this theorem does not define an arbitrary restriction of a singular kernel to a diagonal where the condition fails.

For $F,G\in\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(M)$, let $\deg F$ be the largest degree with nonzero coefficient kernel, with $\deg 0=0$, and define, coefficientwise in $\hbar$,
$$ F\star_W G =\sum_{r=0}^{\min(\deg F,\deg G)} \frac{\hbar^r}{r!} \left\langle F^{(r)}(\phi)\otimes G^{(r)}(\phi),\,W^{\otimes r}\right\rangle. $$
Each term is formed by the distribution product on the $r$ contracted variable pairs and proper pushforward over those pairs, as in [[thm-qftx-wavefront-product]], integrating with the metric density $\mu_g$ in each contracted variable. The sum is finite and defines a member of $\mathcal F_{\mu c}^{\mathrm{poly}}(M)\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$. If $K\in C^\infty(M\times M)$ is symmetric, then
$$ \Gamma_KF(\phi)=\left\langle F^{(2)}(\phi),\chi K\mu_g^{\otimes2}\right\rangle $$
is also a compactly supported polynomial microcausal functional and lowers polynomial degree by two; here $\chi$ is any compactly supported cutoff equal to one near $\operatorname{supp}F^{(2)}(\phi)$.

$$ F\star_W G=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{\eta^k}{k!}\left\langle W^{\otimes k},F^{(k)}(\phi)\otimes G^{(k)}(\phi)\right\rangle . $$
The pairing is over $k$ independent pairs of variables; $W^{\otimes k}$

distributions at coincident points. The sum is finite because the inputs are

invertible with inverse $\alpha_{-K}$, and
$$ \alpha_K(F\star_W G)=\alpha_K(F)\star_{W+K}\alpha_K(G) $$

Assume Countable Choice and use the globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold, density $\mu_g$ and positive-frequency Hadamard relation of [[def-qftx-wavefront-hadamard]]. Let $a\in\mathcal E'(M^p)$ and $b\in\mathcal E'(M^q)$, $p,q\ge0$, be polynomial coefficient kernels whose nonzero wavefront tuples avoid the all-future and all-past causal cones, with zero entries allowed in those cones. Degree-zero kernels are scalars. Label their slots by two distinct original blocks, $A$ and $B$.

Take a finite matching of some of the $p+q$ labelled slots: each slot belongs to at most one edge. Each singular edge joins one slot of $A$ to one slot of $B$, in that order, and has kernel $W$ with $\operatorname{WF}(W)\subseteq\mathcal C_g^+$. Every other edge has a smooth kernel on $M^2$; such an edge may join two slots within either original block or cross between the blocks. No symmetry of these smooth kernels is required for the construction. Multiply $a\otimes b$ by these pulled-back edge kernels and integrate each matched variable against $\mu_g$, retaining the unmatched slots as output variables.

This prescription gives a canonical compactly supported distribution on the unmatched slots. All products and intermediate integrations required by any ordering of these edge contractions are admissible and give the same result as the simultaneous prescription. Here an edge contraction removes its two distinct labelled original slots; no operation duplicates an original coefficient kernel or contracts a removed slot again. The conclusion also includes first contracting smooth edges in each input and then making cross-block singular contractions. The output kernel again avoids the two microcausal cones. Permuting labelled slots or differentiating a finite polynomial functional in external smooth directions gives the corresponding permutation or finite Leibniz expansion of these same kernels.

Consequently all coefficientwise rearrangements of cross-factor $D_W$ contractions and smooth $\Gamma_K$ contractions used in the Hadamard-change formula are canonical on compactly supported polynomial microcausal functionals. This statement does not define a self-contraction $\Gamma_W$ on that class: a mixed future/past wavefront tuple of an individual coefficient need not be transverse to a singular two-point kernel.

Hence $\alpha_K\alpha_{-K}=\alpha_{-K}\alpha_K=I$.

On the regular polynomial subspace of a Euclidean chart, [F4]–[F5] fix the contraction ordering and the factor $\hbar/2$.
